newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak President says goverment acting illegally.
newsitem.headline: Slovak President says goverment acting illegally.

text.p: Slovak President Michal Kovac on Thursday accused the government of Premier Vladimir Meciar of undermining confidence in the rule of law by illegally postponing preparations for a referendum.

Kovac told a news conference that Meciar, his political arch-enemy, had ordered the suspension of preparations for a referendum on direct presidential elections in order to assume presidential powers when Kovac's term expires next March.
"With its decision, the government has shown its disdain for the will of the people and even the basics of our democratic and constitutional system, Kovac said.

The government ordered the suspension of preparations for the presidential referendum pending a ruling by the Constitutional court on whether a change to the constitution through a referendum was legal.
Kovac has set two referendums for May 23 and 24 on direct presidential elections and on whether Slovakia should join NATO. The NATO vote is not affected by the government move.

The NATO referendum was called by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), while the other resulted from a petition initiated by the opposition and signed by some 500,000 voters.
The opposition had called for the presidential referendum in an attempt to prevent Meciar assuming presidential powers when Kovac's term of office expires next March.

In its present composition, the Slovak parliament would be unable to muster the necessary two-thirds majority to elect a new president, which would mean presidential powers would be delegated to the government, effectively to Meciar.
In a television interview on Wednesday Meciar said the differences between the cabinet and Kovac lay in whether it was possible to change the constitution through a referendum.

"If, according to the (new) constitution, the president were directly elected his political credit would change but not his competences," Meciar said. "(The president) would not be subject to any controls, creating a semi-imperial system."
Kovac said the only body with the authority to order the interior ministry to suspend distribution of ballot papers was the multi-party central referendum committee.
